item.research_question: How can the compiled mechanical properties of high entropy alloys (HEAs) and complex concentrated alloys (CCAs) be used to assess their potential as structural materials and guide future development?
item.material_system: 370 high entropy alloys (HEAs) and complex concentrated alloys (CCAs), including 3d transition metal, refractory metal (RHEAs and RCCAs), light metal family, and bronzes and brasses HEAs/CCAs families; HEAs defined as alloys with 5 or more principal elements (5-35 at%); CCAs defined as alloys with 3 or more principal components.
item.processing_route: Compilation of data from published reports from 2004 to 2016; density estimated using rule of mixtures (ROM): ρ=∑xiMi/∑xiVi; Young's modulus estimated using ROM for single phase solid solutions only: E=∑xiEi.
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial loading (tension or compression) at room temperature for 370 alloys; temperature-dependent testing for 27 refractory HEAs (RHEAs).
key_findings: The database covers mechanical properties for 370 HEAs and CCAs reported between 2004 and 2016.
For 27 refractory HEAs, yield stress and elongation are provided as a function of testing temperature.
The database includes alloy composition, microstructure type, density, hardness, yield strength, elongation, ultimate strength, and Young's modulus.
Data entries are organized in a tree-like classification with four families and expanded into classes based on principal element combinations.
The database enables users to browse, search, filter, and plot material property maps using performance indices defined by M. F. Ashby.
item.mechanism: The authors explain that HEAs are presumably stabilized by the configurational entropy of mixing, while CCAs encompass a broader range of alloys with single-phase or multi-phase microstructures; the database allows for the evaluation of performance indices for lighter, stronger, and stiffer structures.
item.limitations: The properties are not equally populated for every alloy due to the lack of literature data.
item.future_work: The database can be used to represent various property spaces, calculate performance indices, and enable data mining to extract insights and uncover patterns to guide and accelerate the development of HEAs and CCAs.
quotes: The database covers the main mechanical properties of HEAs and CCAs tested under uniaxial loading from published reports since 2004 until end of 2016.
The relative merits of these new alloys depend on combinations of properties specific to the applications and loading conditions.
The database can enable data mining to extract insights and uncover patterns to guide and accelerate the development of HEAs and CCAs.
